title: Set Matrix Zeroes
description: If a cell is 0, zero its entire row and column — in place, with O(1) extra space, by using the first row and column as flag arrays.

notes: The trick: reuse row 0 and column 0 as flag arrays, but capture their original zero state in two booleans BEFORE you start writing flags.
Process the interior (i, j >= 1) twice: first pass writes flags, second pass reads flags and zeros cells.
Apply the firstRowZero / firstColZero booleans LAST — otherwise you'd overwrite the flags you still need.

questions.q: Why capture `firstRowZero` and `firstColZero` before scanning the interior?
options: For symmetry with the rest of the algorithm
Because the first row and column get reused as flag storage and would otherwise lose their original zero info
JavaScript needs the booleans for the loops to compile

questions.q: Space complexity of the optimal in-place approach?
options: O(m + n) for two separate flag arrays

questions.q: Why must the first row / first column be zeroed LAST?
options: If you zero them earlier, you destroy the flags the interior pass still needs to read

exercises.prompt: Fill in the flag-capture and final write-back.

blanks.hint: first row index — flag the column

L3.prompt: Write `setZeroes(matrix)` that zeros every row and column containing a 0, using O(1) extra space. Log `JSON.stringify(matrix)` after running on [[0,1,2,0],[3,4,5,2],[1,3,1,5]].
hints: Capture whether row 0 / col 0 originally contained a zero into two booleans.
Use row 0 and col 0 as flags for the interior; apply the captured booleans LAST.
